acceptance: Column-level REFERENCES clauses are removed for Parquet/ORC tables, with a unit test
Registry notes for spark foreign keys stay accurate
context: Found 2026-10-17 during #3080; still reproduces on origin/develop.
description: optimize_spark_table_definition (benchbox/platforms/_spark_helpers.py:257) removes inline PRIMARY KEY (line 278 via _INLINE_PK_RE, line 168) and table-level FOREIGN KEY clauses through _strip_balanced_paren_constraints (line 218; _REFERENCES_TAIL_RE at line 174 only matches after a table-level FOREIGN KEY). A column-level `REFERENCES t(c)` survives. Reproduced on origin/develop: `CREATE TABLE o (k INTEGER NOT NULL, c INTEGER REFERENCES customer(c_custkey), PRIMARY KEY (k))` becomes `CREATE TABLE o (k INTEGER NOT NULL, c INTEGER REFERENCES customer(c_custkey)) USING PARQUET`. The shipped benchmarks declare table-level foreign keys, so nothing fails today, but any benchmark or tuning path that emits column-level REFERENCES would send Spark DDL it may reject. Found while writing the Spark registry notes for #3080.
